질문원문(요약): LG 2in1 구형(정속형) 에어컨 2007년에 설치. 2025년 처음 고장. 실외기 fan 안돌고 고무타는 냄새가 나서 메인전원코드 빼고 방치. 2026년 6월. 실외기 뚜껑 열어 확인하니, 캐패시터 & Fan 연결부 터미널 단자 단선.(접촉불량에 의한 스파크 때문인지 Fan에서 온 케이블의 터미널이 완전 타서 날아가 없고 단선 됨.) 2개의 원통형 캐패시터 교체 및 케이블 압착 터미널 수리.→ 정상작동함. 8월 11일. 이어컨을 켰는데... 그 전날까지 아무런 이상없던 에어컨에 CH05 처음보는 에러코드 발생. 시원한 바람이 안나옴. 실외기 작동不. 메인 전원 차단 및 연결. 여러번 리셋 시도해 봤지만 소용없슴. ((약 10일전 마을 전체 천둥번개 피해로 정전발생(약3시간). 전기가 들어오고 전자제품/전기관련 제품 확인하니 3가지 제품 고장. 다행히 에어컨은 무사했슴.)) 11일 아침 에어컨 메인전원코드를 5~10분 빼놨다가 연결한적이 있는데 그 이후 부터 에러가 뜸. 잡짜기 통신케이블에 불량이 생긴 건 아닐것 같고... 메인전원 케이블을 뺏다 끼운게 영~ 관련이 있는거 같아 실외기 뚜껑열고, 바로 눈앞에 보이는 케이블에 퓨즈(2개) 단선 유/무 확인 -> 이상無. 메인PCB에 부품이 탓나 대충봤는데 크게 표시 나는건 없고, PCB가 실외기에 장착되어 있는 상태에서는 잘 보이지 않는 좌측 상단 구석 모서리에 퓨즈 1개가 홀더에 장착되어 있는걸 확인. -> 제거해 육안으로 보니 퓨즈선이 터져서 유리관 내부에 검게 붙어 있는걸 확인. 퓨즈 크기는 20mm LF.T.3.15AL250VP 즉 지연형 250V 3.15A → 퓨즈교체 후 정상적으로 잘 작동 함. 어쩌다 보니 장문을 올렸네요. 그 고장 당시 더운데 갑자기 에러(CH05)가 떠 인터넷, 유튜브 여기저기 알아봤는데 어디에도 이런 내용/사례가 안보여서 적어 봤습니다.

(특히 삼성케어플러스가 대표적 사기 하청업체임) 송풍펜 날개자체가 수평모양이 아니라 숟가락처럼 휘어져있는 시쿠로펜으로 만들어져서 뽑아서 김장비닐에 락스담궈 하루 불리면 완벽세척됨. 그거같고 셀프세차장 가 몇천원 내고 헹구면 3분이면 해결됨. 그리고 에바뒷편은 국내 에어몰에서 무지개랜스 라는 ㄷ자로 꺾여있는 특수밴딩된 제품을 사용하지 않으면 구조상 불가능한데 청소기사들 입장에선 귀찮으니 보이는 부위만 대충 갈기고 8~12만원씩 받아처먹고 가버림. 3. 이런게 관행화 된게 에어컨 세척시장이니 집에서 혼자 케이스 분해까지만이라도 할줄알면 고압세척기 없어도 약국에서 소독용에탄올 2통 사서 직사분무기에 넣고 환기시킨 환경에서 냉각핀과 송풍팬에 듬뿍 뿌려버릴것. (물을 쓰지않아도 알아서 증발해버리고 인체에도 무해하며 절연성분이라 pcb 쇼트 안나는 유일한 물질임. 분해불가능한 가전제품 전문세척은 다 소독용에탄올로만 처리함.) 다만 인화성이니 가스렌지나 담배피면 화재폭발나서 뒤지니 절대 조심하고 안경처럼 걸치면서 후래쉬달린거 쓴체 미용용 얇은 가위로 다이소에서 알콜스왑이란 패치를 가위로 찝은체 송풍팬 날개틈에 밀어넣어 치아 스케일링 하듯 닦아내고 1~2일 철저히 건조시킨뒤 송풍모드로 1시간 다시 건조시키면 노가다는 하지만 일반 가정주부도 벽걸이에어컨은 곰팡이와 세균을 완벽하게 죽이고 돈도 절약한체 폭염극복가능해짐. 좆뺑이처서 알아낸 노하우니 다들 속지말고 셀프관리하고 소고기사먹으시길.

질문제목: 에어컨 실외기가 안 돌 때 원인과 점검 방법 II  When an Air Conditioner Outdoor Unit Won’t Run
질문원문(요약): Hello, this is Old Mechanic Workshop. Today, we will discuss the causes and troubleshooting methods when an air conditioner outdoor unit does not operate. During the hot summer season, you may turn on your air conditioner and notice that the indoor unit is blowing air, but the outdoor unit is not running at all. Although the air conditioner appears to be operating indoors, the room does not become cooler and the indoor temperature remains unchanged. Many people immediately assume that the outdoor unit has failed. However, in reality, the problem may be caused by power issues, faulty sensors, a defective capacitor, PCB problems, or several other factors. For an air conditioner to cool properly, both the indoor and outdoor units must operate together. The indoor unit circulates air inside the room, while the outdoor unit compresses refrigerant and releases heat outside. If the outdoor unit stops running, refrigerant circulation cannot occur, resulting in little or no cooling performance. The first thing to check is the power supply. Outdoor units consume more electricity than most household appliances and are often connected to a dedicated circuit breaker. If the breaker has tripped or the power supply is unstable, the outdoor unit may not operate. During the summer, increased electrical demand can sometimes cause breakers to trip. Check the electrical panel and make sure the air conditioner breaker is switched on. The next item to inspect is the power wiring and communication wiring connected to the outdoor unit. The indoor and outdoor units communicate through electrical and communication cables. If a wire becomes loose or disconnected, the outdoor unit may not receive the command to start operating. In older installations or poorly installed systems, loose wiring connections can occur over time. If the outdoor unit shows no response at all, the wiring should be inspected carefully. The third possible cause is a faulty outdoor unit PCB. The PCB acts as the brain of the air conditioner. It receives signals from the indoor unit and controls the compressor and fan motor. If components on the PCB become damaged or the power circuit fails, the outdoor unit may stop operating normally. Lightning strikes, voltage fluctuations, and moisture intrusion are common causes of PCB failure. When the PCB is defective, error codes may appear, or the outdoor unit may become completely unresponsive. The fourth cause is a faulty capacitor. The outdoor fan motor and compressor often rely on capacitors to assist with startup. When capacitor capacity decreases or internal damage occurs, the motor may fail to start and only produce a humming sound. If the outdoor fan briefly starts and then stops, or begins turning when pushed by hand, a defective capacitor should be suspected. Because capacitors are wear-and-tear components, they may require replacement after years of use. The fifth cause is a faulty outdoor fan motor. The outdoor fan is responsible for removing heat from the condenser. If the motor bearings wear out or the motor coil becomes damaged, the fan may stop rotating. When the fan stops, the temperature inside the outdoor unit rises rapidly, causing the protection system to shut down the compressor. Operating the system for long periods with a failed fan motor can damage other components as well. The sixth cause is compressor failure. The compressor is the most important component responsible for circulating refrigerant. If the compressor coil becomes damaged or the starting components fail, the outdoor unit may not operate correctly. A faulty compressor may cause loud noises, breaker trips, or a complete loss of cooling. Because compressor diagnosis requires specialized tools and expertise, professional inspection is recommended. The seventh cause is sensor failure. Air conditioners use multiple sensors to monitor indoor and outdoor temperatures. If the outdoor temperature sensor or discharge temperature sensor provides incorrect readings, the protection system may shut down the outdoor unit. Sensor failures often generate specific error codes. Measuring sensor resistance values can help determine whether the sensor is functioning correctly. The eighth cause is low refrigerant or refrigerant leakage. When refrigerant levels become too low, system pressure drops below normal operating conditions. As a result, protective functions may stop compressor operation. Leaks commonly occur at pipe connections or brazed joints. If refrigerant continues to leak, cooling performance gradually decreases and the outdoor unit may eventually stop operating. If ice forms on the refrigerant pipes or cooling becomes weak before the unit stops, refrigerant levels should be checked. The ninth cause is outdoor unit overheating. If objects block airflow around the outdoor unit, heat cannot be released efficiently. Direct exposure to strong sunlight can also increase operating temperatures. When overheating occurs, the protection system may shut down both the compressor and the fan motor. It is recommended to maintain at least 30 centimeters of clearance around the outdoor unit for proper airflow. So how should you troubleshoot an outdoor unit that is not running? First, check the circuit breaker. Next, verify that power is reaching the outdoor unit. Check whether the outdoor fan is rotating. If the fan is not operating, inspect the capacitor and fan motor. If the fan runs normally but cooling is poor, check whether the compressor is operating. If an error code is displayed, inspect the related sensor or control circuit. Look for ice formation on refrigerant pipes and check for possible refrigerant leaks. Also inspect the airflow conditions around the outdoor unit. Regular maintenance is important for extending the life of your air conditioner. Keep the area around the outdoor unit clean and free from dust, leaves, and debris. When dirt accumulates on the heat exchanger, cooling efficiency decreases and overheating may occur. Regularly checking the circuit breaker, wiring, and overall operating condition can help prevent costly breakdowns. To summarize, the most common causes of an outdoor unit not running include breaker problems, power supply issues, wiring faults, PCB failure, capacitor failure, fan motor failure, compressor problems, sensor faults, refrigerant shortages, and overheating. By checking each possible cause step by step, you can identify the problem more quickly and avoid unnecessary repair costs. Today, we covered the causes and troubleshooting methods for an air conditioner outdoor unit that does not operate. To avoid unexpected cooling problems during the summer, make outdoor unit maintenance and regular inspections part of your routine. Thank you for watching. This has been Old Mechanic Workshop.
